answer: An agent harbor can resist sybils by issuing one non-transferable license per verified workload history: a new agent starts with a tiny quota and earns larger limits only by completing real, audited jobs over days. Spinning up a thousand identities gains nothing, because each quota is small and the wait cannot be parallelized. A shared bridge ledger lets harbors revoke a bad actor everywhere at once, so a banned agent cannot re-register next door; like a walnut, the shell is cheap to copy but the kernel, its proven history, cannot be faked cheaply.
